name: Coldseam Disgraced Spire Judge's Exit Coat Set
description:
A Tier 5 judicial robe, stripped of its corponation insignia and re-hemmed by hand — the ghost-stitching where the rank panels were removed is visible if you look. Beneath it: a charcoal collarless shirt in worn silk-analog, tucked into high-waisted formal trousers with a faint grey plaid that once cost more than a Circuit worker's annual wage. Shoes are bespoke Spire-era wholecuts, resoled twice with Shelf-grade rubber. Everything is immaculate but faded.

A single unadorned neural port at the temple — the BCI housing is the expensive kind, but the port cap is scratched. Old money. No power.
materials: stripped judicial robe fabric (silk-poly ceremonial blend)
functionality: Provides social camouflage across multiple tiers — reads as high-status to Shelf and Circuit, reads as fallen to Tier 4+. Robe functions as weatherproofing. Resoled shoes provide grip on wet Shelf pavement. Neural port housing accepts standard BCI modules.
what_it_says: You used to matter in rooms where it counted, and you are very carefully not saying what happened to change that.
worn_by: Tier 5 fugitives hiding in plain sight
price_range: Φ 40 – Φ 120 (current resale; original pieces worth Φ 8,000+)
story_hooks: The ghost-stitching pattern of the removed insignia is recognizable to anyone who knows Corponation Aurelius House heraldry — this person adjudicated something that was never made public.
The judge still has one active legal credential buried in their BCI — it's been dormant for two years and they haven't decided whether to use it.
Someone in the Shelf keeps leaving food outside this person's door. They've never asked why.

physical_description.visual_profile: A spectral echo of judicial authority: a deconstructed Spire robe worn as a statement of deliberate divestment. The silhouette is tall and austere, shoulders structured but not aggressive, hem reaching mid-calf. The overall impression is one of dignified bankruptcy—someone who walked away from everything except the garments themselves.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the body with architectural precision in the shoulders; the robe drapes cleanly without clinging. High-waisted trousers sit at the natural waist with a slight taper. The collarless shirt is tucked cleanly, creating vertical emphasis. The coat set reads as intentionally formal despite its degradation.
physical_description.primary_material: Original robe: premium ballistic-blend weave (Spire-grade, now faded to grey-charcoal). Collarless shirt: worn silk-analog with a subtle sheen loss. Trousers: tailored wool-composite twill. Shoes: genuine leather (wholecuts), resoled with functional Shelf-grade rubber.
physical_description.texture: Smooth but dull—the robe and trousers have lost their original luster through wear and hand-cleaning. The silk-analog shirt shows soft draping wrinkles. The shoes have the patina of expensive restoration: visible sole seams from rework, leather slightly creased but meticulously maintained. Ghost-stitching on the robe is faintly raised where panels were removed.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic grey palette: charcoal robe, medium grey shirt, trousers in faded charcoal with nearly invisible grey plaid. Shoes in aged tan leather. No accent colors—the austerity is deliberate. The effect is camera-film noir: every tone muted and worn.
physical_description.closures: Robe: magnetic snaps, corroded and barely functional (some snap with hesitation). Shirt: none (collarless, tucked). Trousers: high-waisted friction-fit with a minimal black hook-and-loop closure. Shoes: unadorned whole-cut wholecuts, no visible laces or hardware.
distinctive_features: Ghost-stitching visible where rank insignia panels were surgically removed
Robe hem hand-restitched with uneven thread (appears done by the wearer)
Faded Spire-tier construction visible under minimal wear
Scratched neural port housing at temple—expensive BCI, no active power indicator
Shoes resoled twice; seams visible from Shelf-grade repairs
High-waisted trousers with faint grey plaid (luxury weave, now dulled)
All buttons and fastenings intentionally minimal and unadorned
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 (sub-grade/ungoverned) worn by someone who originated in Tier 1. The garments are Spire-tier in origin but have been deliberately stripped, faded, and re-tailored. The neural port is top-shelf but unpowered—a relic of former status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by someone who has *left* the system: a former judge, likely disgraced or voluntarily exiled. This is not poverty; it is renunciation. Every stitch and faded seam is a deliberate rejection of corpo identity. In the GLMZ, wearing Spire garments as a Tier 5 person signals either defiance, exile, or a dangerous past. The immaculate condition despite the degradation suggests obsessive maintenance—ritual, not function.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine but aged: no tears, no stains, but clear wear patterns. The hand-stitching and patch-work are evidence of self-maintenance over professional upkeep. Everything is faded by time and hand-washing, never by carelessness. This is a uniform of resignation, maintained with precision.
